findings.claim: Surah 34:46 quoted as “I advise you only to one thing — that you stand up to Allah in pairs and alone, then reflect.”
findings.truth: The verse says stand up FOR Allah (Khattab: “stand up for the sake of Allah—individually or in pairs—then reflect”; Sahih International: “that you stand for Allah”). “Stand up to Allah” reverses the meaning into opposing Allah.

findings.claim: Question [1] is set as “3 marks — Describe”.
findings.truth: Paper 3 sets two questions, each (a)–(d): outline three (3), explain two (4), explain two with a source of wisdom and authority (5), evaluate (12) — 24 per question, 48 + 3 SPaG = 51. The spec command-word table prices Describe at 4 marks, and Describe is not used on this paper. Relabelled as an outline-three.

findings.claim: Question [4] reads “Discuss this statement”, typed “12 marks — Discuss a Statement”.
findings.truth: The 12-mark command word on this qualification is Evaluate. Discuss does not appear in the spec at all.
findings.evidence: spec command-word table lines 4280–4340; grep for “Discuss” returns no hits

findings.claim: Question [2]: “Explain two differences between the kalam cosmological argument and Aquinas's First Three Ways.”
findings.truth: Aquinas' First Three Ways are named only on the Catholic Christianity and Christianity routes of this paper, not the Islam route, so this question can never be set on 3C. The lesson's misconception panel warning students not to confuse kalam with Aquinas is correct and is left in place; only the exam-form question is re-pointed at the Islam content.
findings.evidence: spec lines 2844 and 3045 (Aquinas named in the Christianity routes); 3C content list lines 3171–3240

findings.claim: “Kitab al-lqtisad fil'ltiqad” in the prose (content twice, exam tip once) — lower-case l where the capital I belongs.
findings.truth: The title is Kitab al-Iqtisad fil'Itiqad, spelled correctly in the same lesson's glossary, knowledge check and flashcards. The error was inherited from the spec PDF extraction.
findings.evidence: internal inconsistency; spec line 3222 shows the same extraction artefact

findings.claim: “is understood as a ayat (sign)” — ayat used as a singular.
findings.truth: Ayat is the plural; the singular is ayah. Not mark-affecting at GCSE, and the definition given (‘signs’) is right.

findings.truth: As F2. Relabelled as an outline-three.

findings.claim: The 12-mark statement is “The Islamic response to suffering is more convincing than the Christian theodicies of Augustine and Irenaeus”, and the mark scheme requires Augustine, Irenaeus and Hick.
findings.truth: Augustine and Irenaeus are named only on the Christianity routes of this paper. The lesson's own exam tip tells students not to import them. A student who prepared this answer would write Christian material into an Islam answer and earn nothing for it. Replaced with an in-route statement on Allah's compassion and suffering, with a mark scheme built from Surah 1, 2:153, 2:155–157 and 2:177.
findings.evidence: spec lines 2857–2858 (Augustine and Irenaeus on the Christianity route); 3C section 1.7–1.8 lines 3225–3240

findings.claim: “Both names appear in the opening of every surah (the Basmala)”.
findings.truth: The Basmala opens every surah except Surah 9 (At-Tawbah).
findings.evidence: settled Qur'anic fact; quran.com/9 shows no Basmala

findings.claim: Surah 2:155–157 quoted as “…some loss in goods, lives and crops — but give glad tidings to those who patiently persevere…”
findings.truth: A composite of standard translations: Yusuf Ali has “the fruits (of your toil)”, not “crops”, and “to Him is our return”. The sense is right and source credit would still be earned, so it is not worth an edit that would force a re-narration.

findings.claim: Question [1] carries a stray “a” key holding a near-duplicate of its “marks” string.
findings.truth: A leftover field from the build. Harmless to the loader, but it should be dropped when the row is next written. The edits format cannot delete a key, so it is recorded rather than fixed.

findings.claim: “all four main schools of law (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) agree on the fundamental permissibility of temporary marriage (mut'ah) being forbidden”.
findings.truth: Garbled, and it reads as if the Sunni schools permit mut'ah. All four Sunni schools hold that mut'ah is forbidden; Twelver Shi'a jurisprudence permits it. The rest of the lesson states this correctly, so the sentence contradicts its own flashcard.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the same lesson's flashcard; spec 3C 2.1 lines 3247–3255

findings.claim: “Surah 4:3 permits it ‘if you fear you cannot be just, then [marry] only one’”.
findings.truth: The quoted clause is the restriction on polygyny, not the condition that permits it. As written a student could read the verse backwards. The quotation itself is accurate.

findings.claim: The description runs to 124 characters.
findings.truth: The validator caps a lesson description at 100 characters, so the row would be rejected on write. Shortened to 88 characters with the same meaning.
findings.evidence: character count; validator limit in the checker brief

findings.claim: Lesson 5 ‘Contraception, Divorce, Gender Equality and Discrimination’ teaches Humanae Vitae, Catholic annulment, the Catechism, theology of the body and women's ordination. Its description begins “Catholic teaching on contraception…”. Every field is Catholic Christianity; there is no Islam content at all.
findings.truth: The lesson body is byte-identical to lesson 5 of the Paper 3 Catholic unit — a duplicated row. The Islam route needs the 3C section 2 content it is missing: contraception and azl with Sahih al-Bukhari 34:432 and 62:136, divorce with Surah 2:226–241 and the Sunni/Shi'a rules for talaq, khul and iddah, roles of men and women with Surah 4 and Surah 2:228, and gender discrimination with Surah 33:35. This is a rebuild, not a patch: five text fields, six practice questions, five knowledge checks, eleven flashcards, seven glossary terms and sixteen narration blocks. Recommendation: pull the lesson from live and rebuild it against 3C 2.5–2.8, then fact-check and re-narrate.
findings.evidence: diff of the two units' raw lesson 5 is empty; spec 3C section 2.5–2.8, lines 3283–3302
findings.ruling: REBUILD ITEM for Tom: wrong-route lesson copied from the Catholic unit; too large to patch in the loop. Other items: fix in the Catholic unit / unverified.

findings.claim: “Catechism 1938 states that ‘every form of social or cultural discrimination in fundamental personal rights on the grounds of sex, race, color… must be curbed and eradicated as incompatible with God's design.’” (repeated in the conclusion, exam tip, practice question [3], knowledge check [3] and the glossary).
findings.truth: That sentence is Catechism 1935; 1938 is the paragraph on sinful inequalities. This matters only if the ruling on F22 is to move this lesson to the Catholic route rather than rebuild it — in that case the paragraph number must be corrected in six places. If lesson 5 is rebuilt as Islam content the error disappears with it, which is why no edit is written here. Verify against the Catechism before moving.
findings.evidence: Catechism of the Catholic Church, para 1935 (quoting Gaudium et Spes 29); not verified online — vatican.va was outside this session's fetch allowance
findings.ruling: REBUILD ITEM for Tom: wrong-route lesson copied from the Catholic unit; too large to patch in the loop. Other items: fix in the Catholic unit / unverified.

summary: Lesson 5 is not an Islam lesson at all: it is a byte-identical duplicate of the Paper 3 Catholic route's lesson 5, so the Islam route currently teaches nothing on contraception, divorce or gender equality in Islam and needs a rebuild (F22). Lessons 1-4 are sound Islam content but carry a misquoted Surah 34:46, two leaks of Christianity-route material (Aquinas, Augustine/Irenaeus) into practice questions, a Basmala over-claim, a garbled mut'ah sentence, and the subject-wide exam-form faults (a 3-mark Describe that does not exist on this paper, and Discuss for the 12-mark Evaluate).
